items.summary: Daily GitHub Actions cron accrues field RUM history passively so the strict ladder flips on evidence cadence, not founder-session cadence.
items.why: The strict perf ladder needs 36 more `/` route samples and accrual currently only happens when a founder session manually runs `npm run rum:pull`. At ~5 samples/day of organic traffic that is weeks of sessions babysitting a data pipe. A scheduled workflow makes the evidence loop self-feeding — the single highest-leverage unlock for the entire LCP saga.
items.recipe: Create `.github/workflows/rum-pull.yml` (daily cron) that runs `npm run rum:pull` and commits `data/rum-history.ndjson` + `data/rum-summary.json` + `.cache/rum-raw` deltas with [skip ci]. Set R2 read credentials as GitHub Actions secrets via `gh secret set` sourced from the secrets gateway (CANON-019 agent work — github.org and cloudflare.r2 are both READY).

items.summary: Deploy-annotated field-performance verdicts: every ship receipt gets auto-graded by subsequent RUM data (pending → improved/regressed/neutral), surfaced publicly.
items.why: S173 shipped the critical-CSS de-dupe but 'field-verify' is currently a human squinting at two JSON files. A comparator that segments rum-history into pre/post-deploy windows turns each deploy into a falsifiable experiment, and grading receipts automatically closes the deploy→field loop forever. Public deploy-annotated perf provenance is something no studio site does.
items.recipe: Create `scripts/compare-rum-windows.mjs --boundary 2026-06-05` emitting per-route median/p75 deltas with sample counts and an honest confidence tier; write `data/field-verdicts.json`; extend the /studio-pulse/ Field Performance strip with a deploy-marker timeline; auto-grade ship receipts with a `fieldVerdict` field updated on every `rum:pull`.

items.summary: Fix the Trusted Types intake parser dropping Reporting-API body fields (80/81 reports are all-null) and add sink clustering so burndown is evidence-driven.
items.why: The soak finally accumulates volume but the forensics are blind: nearly every KV row has null documentUri/sourceFile/lineNumber because the Worker intake only normalizes the legacy `csp-report` shape, not the Reporting API `{type, body:{...}}` shape modern Chrome sends. You cannot burn down sinks you cannot see — this fix multiplies the value of every future soak day.
items.recipe: In `cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js` intake handler, normalize both report shapes (`csp-report` wrapper, Reporting API array with `body.documentURL/sourceFile/lineNumber/sample`); add `scripts/analyze-tt-violations.mjs` clustering reports by sourceFile:line into a burndown table written to `docs/TT_BURNDOWN_<date>.md`; deploy worker and verify intake 204 + a parsed sample.

items.summary: Eliminate the dominant sitewide TT sink: the gtag idle-boot inline script's createElement('script').src assignment, via one narrow allowlisted policy.
items.why: The one parseable violation points at index.html line 15 col 126 — exactly the gtag boot snippet's `s.src=` TrustedScriptURL sink, which fires on every page view sitewide and plausibly accounts for the 78-violation day. Fixing this single sink class collapses most of the burndown in one move and is the gating item before any enforce canary.
items.recipe: Add a tiny head-level policy snippet (or extend the gtag boot IIFE) creating `trustedTypes.createPolicy('vs-loader', {createScriptURL: allowlist(googletagmanager.com, js.stripe.com, *.supabase.co)})` with graceful no-op when trustedTypes is absent; route the gtag `s.src` through it; propagate sitewide via the existing build propagation; rerun `node scripts/probe-tt-soak.mjs` after a soak interval.

items.summary: Read the 5% mobile nav-sheet canary telemetry and emit a graduate/hold/silent verdict instead of letting the canary run unobserved forever.
items.why: The S167 canary has been live for weeks with no readout step — a canary nobody reads is just risk with extra steps. Either telemetry shows usage signal (graduate per the flag-gate memory pattern with founder device verify) or the canary is silent, which is itself a finding that the telemetry sink needs repair.
items.recipe: Create `scripts/check-nav-sheet-canary.mjs` reading `api/nav-sheet-stats.json` + any KV/RUM nav-sheet events; emit verdict artifact `data/nav-sheet-verdict.json` (graduate-ready | hold | telemetry-silent) with evidence counts; surface in the startup brief signals if silent.

items.summary: Hash-key the compact-handoff LLM cache so unchanged handoffs skip the haiku call entirely instead of expiring hourly.
items.why: compact-handoff burned ~3K haiku tokens this session to re-summarize a LATEST_HANDOFF.md that had not changed since the last run — the 1h TTL is time-based when it should be content-based. Small fix, permanent saving on every future session start. Measurement: context-meter ledger byScript shows compact-handoff 3053 tokens today; expected 0 on unchanged-handoff sessions.
items.recipe: In `scripts/compact-handoff.mjs`, key the cache on sha256(LATEST_HANDOFF.md) stored alongside the compact output; skip the LLM call when the hash matches regardless of age; keep a 7d hard ceiling for safety.

items.summary: Turn CANON-007 staging parity green: deploy the current build to staging and close the security-header gap (headerParity false on 3/3 routes, shell stale on 2/3).
items.why: Staging is reachable but lies — it serves a pre-S173 shell on /studio-pulse/ and /membership/ and is missing the CSP/HSTS/XCTO/Referrer-Policy quartet everywhere, so it cannot catch the exact drift class it exists to catch. A yellow parity artifact that stays yellow forever trains everyone to ignore it.
items.recipe: First curl staging headers to confirm which of the 4 sampled headers diverge; sync the current build to the Hetzner staging origin (existing staging deploy path); add the security-header quartet at the staging edge (origin config or staging worker route); rerun `node scripts/check-staging-parity.mjs` and require green.

items.summary: Close the MODULE_NOT_FOUND class for good: add delegation shims for skill-profile.mjs and sample-codebase.mjs, the two protocol scripts that failed this session.
items.why: S172 healed six shims but the heal allowlist missed these two — both failed again at this session's /start and /audit. Every miss costs a failed subprocess, an error block in the transcript, and a manual fallback. The structural-gate memory pattern says extend the heal list, not hand-write one-off shims.
items.recipe: Add `lib/skill-profile.mjs` and `sample-codebase.mjs` to the `check-protocol-scripts.mjs` heal manifest; run `node scripts/check-protocol-scripts.mjs --heal`; verify both resolve (delegating to studio-ops siblings or emitting a clean no-op JSON when the sibling lacks them).

items.summary: Ship the Ark signature-failure dossier upstream as repo-question cargo so studio-ops actually sees the 4 accumulated verification failures.
items.why: The dossier exists locally but CANON-022 makes signature verification studio-ops' surface — a dossier nobody shipped is a finding nobody owns. Four failures now (up from 3) means the failure class is live, not historical.
items.recipe: Run `node scripts/ark.mjs ship --type repo-question --to studio-ops` with payload referencing `docs/ARK_SIGNATURE_FAILURE_DOSSIER_2026-06-04.md`, the 4 failing cargo IDs, and replyTo this slug; log the cargo ID in the handoff.

items.summary: Restore truthful startup-brief signals: Tests shows ?/?, Context age shows ⛔ ?d, Genome shows ? — three data sources the renderer can no longer parse.
items.why: The brief is the sole context source at /start, so every `?` is a hole in the only instrument panel the session gets. The ⛔ on context age is likely a date-parse miss rather than truly stale context, which means the brief is currently crying wolf on its scariest signal.
items.recipe: Trace `render-startup-brief.mjs` reads for tests count, CURRENT_STATE `Last updated:` parse, and genome snapshot; fix the source format or the parser (whichever drifted); re-render and require all three signals to show real values.
